title: Simple Boxed List

illustrates.quote: A list is not preceded by a blank line: ... b. When it follows a top box line. (See Formats, §7, Boxed Material.) (See Sample 8-4: Simple Boxed List on page 8-16.)

blocks.features: Placeholder standing in for running text on the print page that precedes the box, not shown in this excerpt (this book’s own convention; the braille ellipsis "444" that follows it has no print-side input to model from).
Bold heading directly above the boxed list, no blank line beneath it in print.
Boxed list of five questions; each item's opening interrogative word is underlined.
Placeholder standing in for running text on the print page that follows the box (same convention, closing side).

print.printFeatures: Ruled box inside a light-grey shaded panel; bold heading above the box (outside the ruled border); each item's interrogative word underlined.

braille.notes: Line 1 'text 444' is the placeholder for preceding running text; line 2 blank; line 3 the heading ',9t]rogative ,pron\ns' (Interrogative Pronouns); line 4 the top box rule (40 '7's); lines 5-9 the five list items, each opening with the underline-word indicator '_1' before the interrogative word and ending in '8' (question mark); line 10 the bottom box rule (40 'g's); line 11 blank; line 12 ',text 444' resumes the placeholder running text after the box. The list is NOT preceded by a blank line because it follows the top box rule directly (line 4 to line 5), per 8.3.3.b.

resolution: braille.lines byte-identical between A and B. Heading level: both runs stored the raw cell-position "5"; re-derived directly from source .txt (line 6179, ",9t]rogative ,pron\ns") = 4 leading U+2800 blank cells = cell-5 = level 2. Structure: reshaped into an explicit nested `{kind:"box", blocks:[heading, list]}` print block (mirroring Emboss’s own `{type:"box", blocks:[...]}` document-model shape) so buildModel8 can build the top/bottom box-rule pair faithfully — unlike sample-8-13, this box has no un-modelable content inside it, so a full match is plausible here. A’s "text 444" placeholder paragraphs (on both sides of the box, matching this book’s own convention for eliding surrounding running text) are kept; B silently dropped them from print.blocks even though its own braille.notes describes them — A’s more complete structure is used. The "444" braille ellipsis marker itself has no print-side input to build from and is expected to be a documented mismatch on those two lines only.
